Back in the old days (1992), I was one of the original members of a local BBS for Mac enthusiasts. It was an awesome place to talk to some really smart people, even among my teenage contingent. Most of the members were friends from before the BBS was founded. Eventually, the BBS grew so popular that we were getting members from across the country. At some point after a couple of years, we must have reached a critical mass, because the civility we had enjoyed for most of the BBS's existence started to break down. Pretty soon it was flame wars and all-caps name-calling (albeit with a lot of very funny and creative insults... over-educated nerds that we were) all the time.

Like a lot of other members, I got tired of the bickering and moved on to other boards and forums. And I've had to do this over and over again over the past 2+ decades. I've probably been a deeply active member of about a dozen forums over the years. Eventually they all go to hell. It seems like no matter how great the community is at first, after a few years of growing membership, popularity and participation, it reaches a breaking point. Sometimes it's because trolls find it and intentionally stir up trouble. Sometimes it's because an influx of new members changes the ethos of the site somehow and it's just no fun anymore. Sometime it's because management goes off the rails or there's staff turnover that negatively affects the site. Sometimes the people who run the site see dollar signs and neglect running the forums in favour of generating revenue elsewhere on the site. Sometimes it's just some members got into a fight and blew the entire place up with their conflict.

There's no reason for this not to happen to Voat at some point. Especially if it remains as committed to a "free speech at all costs" ideal. At some point, someone is going to found a subverse that blows up the site either legally or among the members. Or a couple of the admins will get in a fight and we'll all feel compelled to take sides. Or they'll "sell out" and a bunch of us will exit in a huff. Or, or, or.... The possibilities are endless. There's nothing special about Voat that guarantees that any of these things won't happen. Not everyone who joins here is going to be aware of what's happened in "the other place," and even some of those who are (like me, although I was not a member "over there" and had no horse in that race) will eventually forget about it, so that's not going to be the glue that binds us to the current vibe of the site forever.

Even technical constraints can only help so much. Sure, there may be no shadowbanning and up/downvoating rules are different, etc. But if someone wants to stir things up, they surely can. And other shit just tends to happen, too, as we all know.

So, maybe the best we can do is enjoy Voat in its current form while it lasts. That's what I intend to do, anyway.
